text:
maya: quick sync — we're trying to tighten scan ownership and evidence handling for SAST/DAST findings in the monorepo. current CODEOWNERS is 70% accurate and noisy. looking for an approach that ties findings -> team -> encrypted evidence bucket. any strong opinions?

liam: +1 on mapping table. CODEOWNERS is good for PR signals but not for vuln ownership. we need a small ownership manifest per service.

simon: can we keep it lightweight? a yaml next to service manifest with `security_team` and `triage_channel`. example: 
```
service.yaml:
  name: payments
  owners: [@payments-platform]
  security_team: payments-security
  triage_channel: #payments-ops
```
That lets automation route tickets.

maya: that looks great. then pipeline can create a ticket with evidence link. question: where should evidence live? we want auditability + encryption with customer CMK-like controls for sensitive code paths.

anna: DAST artifacts are huge. for SAST it's compact (files + stack trace). I'd suggest a central S3 bucket with prefixes per-team and per-run, encrypted with a KMS key per-org/team. retention policy 90 days by default, 1 year for security SLA cases.

liam: agree re: prefixes. example prefix: `s3://scan-evidence/<team-slug>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/run-<id>/` and store `finding-<id>.json` plus `repro.sh` if present. Use CMKs and log key usage to audit-log.

sec-bot: FYI: when evidence is uploaded, the scanbot will emit an audit event: `scan.evidence.upload` with fields {run_id, finding_id, uploader, kms_key_id, s3_path}. This is already ingested into Splunk.

maya: perfect. second concern: external scanners (3rd-party DAST) need temporary read access to the evidence bucket for verification. we want ephemeral RBAC grants with TTL and audit trail. how do others handle ephemeral grants?

simon: give them a short-lived STS role with scope-limited policy: read to `s3://scan-evidence/<team-slug>/run-<id>/*`. log role assumption and rotate credentials. automate revoke after TTL.

liam: + enforce MFA and require a signed justification in the ticket before ephemeral role is created. reduces noise and gives traceability.

anna: about false positives — can we standardize a triage label set so scan->ticket automation adds metadata: severity, confidence, reproducibility, fingerprint. Then triage playbook can auto-close low-confidence ones after 14 days if owner ack not required.

maya: proposed labels: `sec/severity:{critical,high,medium,low}`, `sec/confidence:{high,medium,low}`, `sec:triage-state:{untriaged,investigating,fp,accepted}`. automation should attach the scanner fingerprint to prevent duplicate tickets.

sec-bot: note: the scanner fingerprinting currently hashes file path + line + rule-id. we can extend to include repo-commit to make it run-specific.

liam: operational question — who gets paged for a 'critical' new finding in prod? currently pager duty goes to security-oncall but we could create per-product emergency chains. thoughts?

maya: keep security-oncall as the first responder, but allow product teams to subscribe to high-severity alerts for their services after initial ack. security handles TTR SLA.

ops-oncall: from an oncall POV: we need clear playbooks in the ticket template. include runbook links, rollback checklist, and contact matrix. also add a `run_id` and direct evidence link in the PD alert.

anna: small FYI: CI is creating a ton of noise for `TODO`-like rules. suggest a non-blocking tag for 'comment-only' that surfaces in dashboard but doesn't block premerge. helps dev velocity.

maya: implementation plan draft: 1) define ownership manifest schema (short YAML) 2) update scanbot to use manifest to route tickets 3) central S3 evidence prefix + CMK per-team 4) ephemeral STS role generator + MFA + justification check 5) ticket label normalization + fingerprinting 6) update oncall runbooks and PD alerts.

liam: timeline? I can take 1 & 2. Simon can do infra for 3 & 4. Anna can own label normalization and triage playbook.

simon: estimate 2 sprints for infra pieces (bucket policy, KMS key proposals, STS lambda, audit hooks). will open infra RFC tomorrow.

maya: cool. I'll draft a short RFC for the manifest and the triage labels. will post in #eng-security for review. after RFC we can wire up automation.

sec-bot: action created: RFC-1234 (scan-ownership-manifest) assigned to maya, due 7 days.

ops-oncall: please include a sample PD payload in the RFC. saved us time during last incident.

maya: will do — sample PD payload + example `s3_path` + KMS metadata. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
